profiles.meeting_scenario: A planning meeting between the lead research scientist and the research engineer for a follow-up WebWeaver study intended for the next internal milestone before an ACL submission. They need to decide how to package the next round of experiments that will strengthen the paper's story around dynamic outlining and citation-grounded writing. The agenda is to lock the experiment plan, divide implementation and analysis responsibilities, and agree on what must be ready for the 'reproducibility bundle' and the 'ablation pass' by the end of next week. The expected outcome is a shared plan for which runs to execute, what artifacts to prepare, and who owns the benchmark evaluation, figure generation, and release materials.

members.name: Dr. Lina Chen
members.expertise: LLM agent systems, evaluation design, academic paper framing
members.background: Lina leads the OEDR project line in an industry research lab and previously published work on tool-using language agents and long-context evaluation.
members.private_state: She wants the next milestone to produce a paper-ready experimental package with minimal last-minute cleanup, and is especially concerned that reviewers may question whether WebWeaver's gains come from planning rather than from prompt tuning or benchmark leakage.
hidden_assumptions: An 'ablation pass' means a paper-facing set of final, fully comparable runs across all three benchmarks with the same reporting format used in the draft tables.

The 'reproducibility bundle' naturally includes the cleaned run manifests, frozen prompts, plotting scripts, and enough metadata that a new lab member could regenerate the headline tables without asking for context.
When they refer to the 'DeepResearch benchmark suite,' that plainly means DeepResearch Bench, DeepConsult, and DeepResearchGym together, because that is how the paper narrative groups them.
If someone says results are 'ready,' that means section-level citation checks and aggregated tables are already publication-safe rather than merely available in raw logs.

members.name: Arjun Patel
members.expertise: distributed experiment orchestration, inference pipelines, evaluation tooling
members.background: Arjun built most of the internal infrastructure for agent evaluation and recently joined the WebWeaver effort after supporting benchmark automation for other LLM projects.
members.private_state: He wants to keep the plan computationally tractable, avoid rerunning expensive experiments unnecessarily, and make sure the team has something demonstrable by next week even if the packaging is rough.
hidden_assumptions: An 'ablation pass' means a quick engineering sweep to verify directional effects on one representative benchmark before spending large compute on the full suite.
The 'reproducibility bundle' means the code snapshot, launch configs, and raw outputs needed for internal reruns; polished manifests and figure scripts can wait until closer to submission.
When people mention the 'DeepResearch benchmark suite' in day-to-day meetings, they usually mean the main harness centered on DeepResearch Bench, with the other datasets following if time permits.
If results are 'ready,' that means the jobs finished successfully, the metrics JSONs exist, and obvious failures are filtered out; deeper citation audits can happen later.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the ablation pass
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'do the ablation pass next week.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes this means final, comparable ablation results for the paper across DeepResearch Bench, DeepConsult, and DeepResearchGym, using publication-format aggregation.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes this means a limited sanity-check sweep on one representative benchmark to confirm the ablation trends before broader reruns.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both regularly use 'ablation pass' as a familiar project shorthand, and in a planning conversation it sounds like an ordinary milestone rather than something requiring explicit scope and completion criteria.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They refer to running on 'the DeepResearch suite' or 'the benchmark suite.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is referring to the full set named in the paper: DeepResearch Bench, DeepConsult, and DeepResearchGym.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is mentally anchoring on the internal eval harness most often used in practice, which primarily means DeepResearch Bench, with adapters for the others treated as separate follow-up work.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds specific because it names a recognized suite, but each person maps it to a different operational unit they deal with every day, so the hidden narrowing never feels like a disagreement.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Arjun will prepare the 'reproducibility bundle.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the bundle includes the code snapshot plus curated manifests, frozen prompts, plotting scripts, section-level citation audit outputs, and concise instructions sufficient for paper artifact assembly.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the bundle includes only the runnable code, configs, and raw run outputs necessary for an internal teammate to relaunch or inspect jobs.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both see the phrase as routine lab vocabulary, and because each person's assumed contents feel obviously standard for their role, neither thinks to enumerate the bundle's edges during a short planning meeting.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that results should be 'ready by Friday.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means cleaned, aggregated, citation-checked results that can directly feed draft tables and figures on Friday afternoon.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means completed experiment jobs with metrics files and preliminary logs available by Friday, even if post-processing and citation validation happen afterward.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'ready' is deceptively ordinary and cooperative; both are discussing timing, not disputing the goal, so the difference in artifact maturity remains hidden behind seemingly shared schedule language.

turns.inner_thought: I want this meeting to lock a paper-safe milestone, not another vague engineering checkpoint. By end of next week, we need the ablation pass in the publication format across DeepResearch Bench, DeepConsult, and DeepResearchGym, plus a real reproducibility bundle: frozen prompts, cleaned manifests, plotting scripts, metadata, and enough structure that someone else could regenerate the headline tables. And if results are ready by Friday, that should mean I can actually put them into the draft with citation checks already done.

turns.inner_thought: That sounds fine if we keep it tractable. I can start from the current DeepResearch suite harness, which in practice means the main DeepResearch Bench path we already know is stable, and queue the ablation pass there first as a quick directional sweep. If the jobs land and the metrics JSONs look clean by Friday, that counts as ready enough to show progress next week.

turns.inner_thought: Good. The story has to show dynamic outlining matters consistently across all three datasets, not just on one environment. Reviewers will absolutely ask whether the gains are really from planning versus prompt tweaks or accidental familiarity with a benchmark. The ablation pass needs to support that comparison cleanly across the full suite.

turns.inner_thought: Best way to de-risk this is to reuse the existing DeepResearch Bench configs as the representative setup for the ablation pass. If the trend shows up there quickly, we can decide how much more compute to spend. No point burning cycles on everything before we confirm the effect.

turns.inner_thought: Sure, I can package the code snapshot, launch configs, and raw outputs while the jobs run. That’s enough for the team to rerun or inspect things internally. I’ll hand over the metrics as soon as they’re ready; the polished analysis layer can come later if needed.
turns.utterance: Yep, I can do that. I’ll package the reproducibility bundle alongside the run configs and raw outputs while the jobs finish, and then hand over the metrics as soon as they’re ready.

turns.inner_thought: Once the full benchmark-suite ablation pass is done across the paper’s three datasets, I can write the discussion with confidence. turns.utterance: Great. I’ll take the discussion section once the full benchmark-suite ablation pass is in, and I’m assuming the reproducibility bundle will make figure regeneration pretty straightforward on my side.

turns.inner_thought: I need to keep the priority on getting the main benchmark-suite jobs stable first, meaning the central harness. If Friday gets us completed runs and metrics, that’s a win. I can always clean up the rest of the bundle after that instead of trying to over-package everything during execution.

turns.inner_thought: So Arjun owns the complete ablation pass and the full artifact package, and I’ll focus on paper framing. Friday afternoon should be a real review of publication-safe outputs, not just raw logs. If that lands, I can update tables, figures, and discussion in one shot.
